messages:
jamal: Hey sec team — got an email from payroll@vendorcorp.com asking me to 'confirm bank details' for Redwood invoice. Looks branded. Link: https://vendorcorp.invoices/redwood/confirm. I did NOT click. pls advise
carla-ops: thanks @jamal — can you forward raw email to security@redwood.com and paste the full headers here? also screenshot of the message for context :eyes:
jamal: forwarded raw to security@ and pasted headers below:
```
Received: from mail.vendorcorp.com (mail.vendorcorp.com [198.51.100.22])
From: "Vendor Corp Payroll" <payroll@vendorcorp.com>
Subject: Action required: confirm bank details
Return-Path: bounced@vendor-notify.com
Authentication-Results: mx.redwood.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=vendorcorp.com; dkim=pass header.d=vendorcorp.com
```
carla-ops: header looks like SPF/DKIM passing, but note Return-Path differs. could be a compromised upstream. @sec-bot run sandbox/url analysis on the link
sec-bot: sandbox report (automated): verdict=malicious, category=credential-phish, payload=hosted login form that POSTs creds to http://45.77.13.9/collect, redirect chain: vendorcorp.invoices -> tinyurl[.]link/rd123 -> 45.77.13.9. No malware binary detected.
mike-harper: quick checks: DNS for vendorcorp.invoices is an A record pointing to a CDN but tinyurl redirect is suspicious; ASN for 45.77.13.9 is a VPS provider often abused for phishing. DKIM/SPF can be forged or abused via compromised vendor mail system.
alice.ng: curl -I shows 302 through tinyurl, final landing page contains HTML form with company logos and hidden iframe. form action posts to http://45.77.13.9/collect. no JS obfuscation beyond basic base64. saving screenshots and html snip to the triage ticket.
carla-ops: recommended actions:
- Quarantine incoming mail from *.invoices@vendorcorp.com and block the tinyurl redirect patterns at the proxy.
- Notify vendor security contact immediately (secops-liaison, can you reach out?)
- Create SIEM/IDS rule for POSTs to 45.77.13.9 and similar VPS IPs used in redirects.
- Communicate to staff: targeted phish alert with indicators, instruct to not click and to forward to security@redwood.com.
secops-liaison: reaching out to vendor security now. sending them headers, sandbox output, and IOCs. asked for confirmation if this is from their system or a compromise.
jamal: I did not interact with the link, no creds entered. appreciate the quick turnaround.
carla-ops: containment steps executed: updated inbound mail rule to quarantine messages with vendorcorp.invoices in URL, added tinyurl[.]link pattern to proxy blocklist, SIEM rule created for POST to 45.77.13.9. will escalate if vendor confirms legit.
mike-harper: recommend we also push a short org-wide reminder about verifying vendor domains and suspicious links, plus add a KB entry showing how to inspect headers and send to security.
sec-bot: note: attachment scan result = clean (no binaries). verdict remains credential-phish.
carla-ops: follow-ups: 1) vendor response expected within 2 hours, 2) awareness blast drafted (will post after vendor confirmation to avoid noise), 3) update blocklist with final IOCs, 4) ticket created: SEC-2026-482 (triage + IOC tracking). tagging for post-incident writeup if vendor confirms compromise.
jamal: thanks y'all. appreciate the quick containment. :thumbsup:
carla-ops: closing thread for now — will re-open if vendor disputes or more hits come in. documented actions and artifacts in SEC-2026-482.
